newsitem.title: MEXICO: Mexico stocks inch up at close after slow session.
newsitem.headline: Mexico stocks inch up at close after slow session.

text.p: Mexican stocks closed up very slightly in a late fillip after drifting sideways in thin dealings for most of the session.
"Prices held steady, and gained a little towards the close on month-end buying. Nothing special happened, as you would expect in a consolidation period like this one," said a trader.

The blue chip IPC index closed up 4.25 points, or 0.13 percent, at 3,273.09. Volume was a lackluster 50.1 million shares traded, and that figure was inflated by 17 million shares of cross trades in just two stocks.
Dealers noted that trade was slowed considerably by U.S. stocks markets closing for Thanksgiving, and by the Mexican Stock Exchange suspending open outcry to test an electronic trading system.
"I liked the session, trade was interesting, even though the excitement and flavor of the outcry was lost," the broker added.
A total of 100 stocks were traded, of which gainers outnumbered losers by 49 to 30.
Autoparts maker Iasasa headed the gainers, up four centavos to 37, following a debt restructuring plan.

Publishing company Gfesa bounced back from a fall on Wednesday to end second on the gainers' list, up 17 centavos at 1.83, which some traders put down to expectations the firm would finalize a pending deal with Bankers Trust.
Food company Herdez headed the losers, down ten centavos at 2.30 pesos.

Dealers noted most trade was in stocks that do not have ADRs in New York. Market heavyweight Telmex, normally top of the most-traded stocks list in Mexico, ended in a lowly and almost unheard-of sixth place on Thursday.
